summary: Spanish-built 1887 light on Caja de Muertos (Coffin Island) off Ponce; US Lighthouse Service keepers 1901-1947; automated 1945; reserve rebuilding.

structures.note: Cylindrical tower in the center of the keepers' building. 62 ft (19 m) including the lantern per NRHP and EnciclopediaPR; 41 ft from base to lantern center per the 1901 report and the USLHS record.

access.note: Reserve closed to the public except its beaches after Hurricane Maria (2017), per a 2021 report; reserve rebuilding still in progress in 2026.

facts.agency: US Coast Guard (light, per 2026 report); Puerto Rico Department of Natural and Environmental Resources (reserve)

corrections.why: A 2026 report describes the lights as under Coast Guard jurisdiction (federal); the reserve on the island is run by the Puerto Rico DRNA.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 1901 report says works began in 1882 and were finished in 1885. The nomination gives 1887 as the build year. EnciclopediaPR says the light began operating on 15 August 1887 and dates the original lantern to 1885. The Society's record gives 1887 for the original lens installation. The sources do not explain how the 1885 and 1887 dates relate.

The 1901 report and the USLHS record give 41 feet (12.5 m) from base to the lantern center; the nomination and EnciclopediaPR give 62 feet (19 m) including the lantern. Not reconciled by the sources; the story gives both.

The cached OCR of the Commissioner's report reads 'June lo'. The page image (scan p. 751, printed p. 51) reads 'On June 13, 1922', matching the 1922 Bulletin's 'on June 13'. The earlier 10 June reading was an OCR error.

EnciclopediaPR says the island is eight miles from the municipality of Ponce; the nomination places the light about seven miles east of the entrance to Ponce Harbor. Not reconciled; the story gives both.

notes_for_editor: Roster names come from the USLHS place page (NARA registers via Kraig Anderson); matched by position in the archive's own roster; names are as printed. Roster has two principal keepers overlapping 1945-46. Severo del Olmo and Cesar Prieto rest on a single source (EnciclopediaPR). The 1922 first-aid date was checked against the Commissioner's page image (scan p. 751, printed p. 51): it reads 'On June 13, 1922'; the cached OCR 'June lo' was an error, and the Bulletin also says June 13. The 1917 Bulletin passage (14 November) and the 1924 passage (10 December) do not state the year; the story gives the year only where the source does. The 1915 Bulletin's 'iii' and 'Jigh:' are OCR errors in the quote. The 1926 Bulletin page image (PDF p. 33) confirms 7 persons, 20 persons and 12 children; the shipwrecked boat's name is legible in the image (Pluma del Mar) but is not used. Light characteristic conflict: 1901 report says a white flash every three minutes; the nomination says every 3 seconds; the record's current Fl W 30s is not confirmed by any source read here. The 1901 Light-House Board entry is printed pp. 77-78 (scan pp. 105-106); the earlier citation to p. 80 was the report's index and is withdrawn. Distance from Ponce: EnciclopediaPR eight miles; NRHP about seven miles east of the entrance to Ponce Harbor (both in the story). The NRHP listing year (1981) appears only in the record and was removed from events. Tesoros de la Isla blog (claims a 1883 royal order, a 1923 tower raise to 19 m, and a 1940 US Navy eviction) is unverified and not used. Wikipedia is a lead only and not cited. Current public access to the tower is not stated by any source; the story says so plainly. The LHB 1901 OCR of the 'Muertos' entry was read directly from the cached text. Newspaper search (Chronicling America, 'Muertos' + 'Ponce', 1887-1915) returned too many unrelated hits to use.
